latest_release.name: v2.0.0 - The Long Hold
latest_release.body:
![Solid 2.0 - The Long Hold](https://www.solidjs.com/img/blog/solid-2-0-the-long-hold/header.png)

# Solid 2.0 is here

5 years is a long time to work on anything. Solid 1.0 bet on signals at a time when fine-grained reactivity was a rare position. Today you will find it in Angular, Svelte, Vue Vapor and a TC39 proposal. Solid 2.0 takes the next step, and today it reaches stable.

### 📣 [Read the announcement: Solid 2.0 - The Long Hold](https://www.solidjs.com/blog/solid-2-0-the-long-hold/)

## What 2.0 brings

- **Async in the graph.** A computation can return a Promise or an async iterator, and everything downstream just handles it. Race conditions are taken care of, optimistic state rolls back so the server stays the source of truth, and `live()` streams server functions over persistent connections. Adding async does not mean refactoring your app.
- **Built to be written by agents.** A fine-grained graph knows exactly what was read, where, and what will update. Development builds report reactive mistakes with a stable code, a source location and a fix, and the same graph catches waterfalls, runaway effects and fan-out that will not scale.
- **One framework for all.** Solid 2.0 ships primitives, not a single blessed stack. What a metaframework needs now lives in core and in framework-agnostic Vite plugins, so bring the router and cache you like.
- **Less is more.** More capability, smaller API. `createResource`, `batch`, `startTransition`, `on`, `produce`, `createComputed` and `createMutable` are gone. Safe by construction rather than by exhaustion.

## The road here

The [Road to 2.0](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/discussions/2425) was announced in February 2025, followed by the [beta](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/discussions/2596) and the [release candidate](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/discussions/2995). Since the API froze we shipped 23 release candidates in 14 weeks, merged 971 pull requests and closed 753 issues. The bar for stable was a full week with no regression in ordinary app code, and no crash or hang anywhere.

Solid has always been bigger than its core team, and 2.0 is the clearest proof of that yet. Thank you to every contributor, tester and sponsor who believed in the project.

## Get started

```sh
npm create solid@latest
```

- [Documentation](https://docs.solidjs.com)
- [Tutorial](https://docs.solidjs.com/tutorial)
- [Migrating from Solid 1.x](https://docs.solidjs.com/migration/from-solid-1)
- [Playground](https://playground.solidjs.com)
- [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/solidjs)

Still on Solid 1.x? It lives on the [`1.x` branch](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/tree/1.x), on npm as `solid-js@v1-latest`, with docs at [v1.solidjs.com](https://v1.solidjs.com).

Solid 2.0 is here. Let's build.

**Full changelog:** [packages/solid/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/blob/main/packages/solid/CHANGELOG.md)

[![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/solidjs/solid/main-ci.yml?branch=main&logo=github&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/actions/workflows/main-ci.yml) [![Coverage Status](https://img.shields.io/coveralls/github/solidjs/solid.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://coveralls.io/github/solidjs/solid?branch=main) [![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/solid-js.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/solid-js) [![](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/solid-js.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/solid-js) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/722131463138705510?style=for-the-badge)](https://discord.com/invite/solidjs) [![Subreddit subscribers](https://img.shields.io/reddit/subreddit-subscribers/solidjs?style=for-the-badge)](https://www.reddit.com/r/solidjs/) **[Website](https://www.solidjs.com/) • [Docs](https://docs.solidjs.com/) • [Tutorial](https://docs.solidjs.com/tutorial) • [Playground](https://playground.solidjs.com/) • [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/solidjs)** Solid is a declarative JavaScript library for building user interfaces. Instead of a Virtual DOM, it compiles templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactivity. Declare your state and use it throughout your app — when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it re-runs. ## At a glance ```tsx import { createSignal } from "solid-js"; import { render } from "@solidjs/web"; function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0); const doubled = () => count() * 2; // The component body runs once. Only `{doubled()}` updates when count changes. return ; } render(() => , document.getElementById("app")!); ``` Try it in our [Playground](https://playground.solidjs.com/).
Explain this! Solid compiles your JSX to real DOM operations at build time. The component function runs once on mount; reactivity is per-expression, not per-render. The `{doubled()}` expression compiles to a tracked update that only touches that one DOM position when `count()` changes. ```js import { template, delegateEvents, insert } from "@solidjs/web"; import { createSignal } from "solid-js"; const _tmpl$ = /*#__PURE__*/ template(`
## Key features - Fine-grained updates to the real DOM — no virtual DOM diff. - Declarative reactive primitives (`createSignal`, `createMemo`, `createStore`). - Render-once components — your component function is plain JavaScript that runs once. - Automatic dependency tracking — reading reactive state subscribes to it. - Microtask-batched updates with `flush()` for synchronous interop. - First-class async: any computation can return a `Promise`/`AsyncIterable`; `` is the boundary. - Optimistic UI primitives (`createOptimistic`, `createOptimisticStore`) and structured `action(...)` mutations. - Streaming SSR and progressive hydration. - TypeScript-first, JSX-first, web-component friendly. - Universal: write custom renderers via [`@solidjs/universal`](packages/universal) to target non-DOM platforms. ## Quick start Start from a [template](https://github.com/solidjs/templates): ```sh npx degit solidjs/templates/solid-v2/basic my-app cd my-app npm install npm run dev ``` Or add Solid to an existing Vite project: ```sh npm i solid-js @solidjs/web npm i -D vite @solidjs/vite-plugin ``` ```js // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; import solid from "@solidjs/vite-plugin"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [solid()] }); ``` and point TypeScript at the web JSX types: ```json { "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "preserve", "jsxImportSource": "@solidjs/web" } } ``` `solid-js` owns renderer-neutral component types, while renderer packages such as `@solidjs/web` and `@solidjs/h` own their JSX namespaces and `jsx-runtime` type entries. ### Coming from Solid 1.x? Read the [migration guide](documentation/solid-2.0/MIGRATION.md). Solid 1.x is maintained on the [`1.x` branch](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/tree/1.x), installs with `npm i solid-js@v1-latest`, and its docs are at [v1.solidjs.com](https://v1.solidjs.com). ## For LLMs / AI assistants The public API differs from any Solid examples that predate 2.0. Before generating Solid 2.0 code, read: - [`packages/solid/skills/solid-2.0/SKILL.md`](packages/solid/skills/solid-2.0/SKILL.md) — the primer: the three rules that matter most, the 1.x → 2.0 corrections, and the primitives to reach for, in under 8 KB. - [`packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md`](packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md) — one-page reference; the bottom enumerates patterns that changed from 1.x. - [`documentation/solid-2.0/MIGRATION.md`](documentation/solid-2.0/MIGRATION.md) — full migration guide. - [docs.solidjs.com](https://docs.solidjs.com) — the docs, with `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. The primer and the cheatsheet ship inside the `solid-js` npm package (`node_modules/solid-js/skills/solid-2.0/SKILL.md`, `node_modules/solid-js/CHEATSHEET.md`; the build also emits the cheatsheet as the `solid-2.0-cheatsheet` skill). The packages carry the `tanstack-intent` keyword, so skill registries that scan `node_modules` find them. ## Repository This is a PNPM workspaces monorepo. The core runtime (`solid-js`, `@solidjs/signals`, `@solidjs/web`, `@solidjs/universal`, `@solidjs/diagnostics`) always shares one version. The two compilers share a version when they release together, and `@solidjs/h`, `@solidjs/html` and `@solidjs/element` version on their own. | Package | Path | Purpose | | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `solid-js` | `packages/solid` | Core runtime — components, flow controls, context, hydration. | | `@solidjs/signals` | `packages/signals` | Reactive primitives — signals, memos, effects, stores. | | `@solidjs/web` | `packages/web` | Web platform runtime — `render`, `hydrate`, SSR, `Portal`, `dynamic`. | | `@solidjs/h` | `packages/h` | Hyperscript / JSX factory. | | `@solidjs/html` | `packages/html` | Build-less tagged template literals. | | `@solidjs/universal` | `packages/universal` | Universal runtime for custom renderers. | | `@solidjs/element` | `packages/element` | Web Components wrapper. | | `@solidjs/compiler` | `packages/compiler` | Native Oxc JSX compiler. | | `@solidjs/babel-plugin` | `packages/babel-plugin` | Babel plugin for JSX compilation. | | `@solidjs/diagnostics` | `packages/diagnostics` | Dev-only diagnostics and attribution harness for tests and agents. | Runtime DOM operations live in `@solidjs/web` (and `@solidjs/universal` / `@solidjs/h` / `@solidjs/html`). The JSX compilers and the DOM runtime live in this repo, so file their issues here, not on [DOM Expressions](https://github.com/ryansolid/dom-expressions). The API reference in one page is [`packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md`](packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md), and the design notes are under [`documentation/solid-2.0/`](documentation/solid-2.0/). ## Why Solid? ### Performant Engineered for performance with years of research behind it — Solid's runtime cost is close to optimized vanilla JavaScript on the [JS Framework Benchmark](https://krausest.github.io/js-framework-benchmark/current.html). Small, fully tree-shakable, fast on the server too. ([Read more](https://dev.to/ryansolid/thinking-granular-how-is-solidjs-so-performant-4g37) about Solid's performance.) ### Powerful Performant state management is built in (Context, Stores, Projections). Async is a first-class capability of computations, with `` / `` boundaries and `isPending` for revalidation indicators. Full SSR, streaming, and progressive hydration when you're ready to move to the server. ### Pragmatic Components are plain functions. Rendering is determined by how state is used — no rendering system to learn. Read-write segregation is encouraged but not enforced. ### Productive Built on JSX and TypeScript, integrates with the Vite ecosystem. Bare-metal abstractions give you direct access to the DOM. Growing ecosystem of [primitives](https://github.com/solidjs-community/solid-primitives), [component libraries](https://kobalte.dev), and build-time utilities. ## More - [Documentation](https://docs.solidjs.com) - [Tutorial](https://docs.solidjs.com/tutorial) - [Examples](examples/) - [Playground](https://playground.solidjs.com/) ## Browser support SolidJS Core supports the last 2 years of modern Firefox, Safari, Chrome, and Edge (desktop and mobile). IE and similar sunset browsers are not supported. For server environments, Node LTS, the latest Deno, and Cloudflare Worker runtimes are supported. ## Community Come chat on [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/solidjs). Solid's maintainers are active there, and we're always looking for contributions. ### Contributors ### Open Collective Support us with a donation and help us continue our activities. [[Contribute](https://opencollective.com/solid)] ### Sponsors Become a sponsor and get your logo on our README on GitHub with a link to your site. [[Become a sponsor](https://opencollective.com/solid#sponsor)]
